problem:
The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
v=⟨{t}^{3}+2,\,6\sqrt{t}+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the **magnitude** of the resultant force, in newtons, acting on the particle when $t=1\,\text{s}.$ Round your final answer **to the nearest integer**.

The magnitude of the resultant force is
{{field-1}} $\,N.$
worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(6\sqrt{t}+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2},\,\frac{3}{\sqrt{t}}+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =2\cdot ⟨3{t}^{2},\,\frac{3}{\sqrt{t}}+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨6{t}^{2},\,\frac{6}{\sqrt{t}}+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=1\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1) & =⟨6(1)^{2},\,\frac{6}{\sqrt{1}}+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,6+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of $F(1)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}|F(1)| & =\sqrt{(6)^{2}+{(6+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(1))}^{2}} \\  & ≈10,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

So, the magnitude of the resultant force is $10\,\text{N}.$
